title: Formalize review owners and acceptance checklist for Private deployment scope change
creator: Jordan Patel
description:
Context: The current PRD for Private deployments was expanded to include an on-prem upgrade path and an updated RBAC model after stakeholder feedback. This change touches runtime upgrade tooling, customer-facing upgrade UX in Console, and contractual obligations for audit/log retention. We need a clear, auditable gating and owner matrix so that PRD sign-off proceeds smoothly across Eng, Design, and Legal without repeated rework.

Goal: Define explicit review owners, a minimal acceptance checklist per discipline, escalation paths for unresolved trade-offs, and a batched approval schedule aligned to the release milestone (private-2026.04). This ticket coordinates the cross-team alignment and tracks outstanding blocking items so PM can record final PRD signoff artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Eng sign-off: Performance regression <= 5% on the serving runtime for on-prem upgrade flows with standard test-suite (link to infra benchmark dashboard), or documented rollback plan with SLO impact and mitigation steps.

Design sign-off: Console upgrade flow mockups validated for primary upgrade path and fallback UX; accessibility checklist completed (WCAG AA); a short validated copy for all customer-facing messaging.
Legal sign-off: Data residency / retention matrix confirmed for on-prem customers; updated contract clause drafted for auditability and passed initial Legal review.
Security sign-off: KMS/HSM integration patterns documented and threat model reviewed by Security, with an action list for outstanding gaps.
Operational sign-off: Runbook for upgrades (preflight checks, rollback, monitoring playbooks) published and verified in runbook repo; on-call escalation path confirmed.
Cross-team gating: All discipline approvals recorded in the PRD Confluence page with timestamps and named approvers before cutting release branch.
updates: 2026-03-10 Jordan Patel: Created ticket after stakeholder alignment call. Captured initial concerns: runtime perf, Console UX, legal retention language.
2026-03-11 Riley Chen: Added tentative owners for each review area: ENG -> Priya Nair, DES -> Alex Morgan, LEGAL -> Samir Desai, SEC -> Nina Park. Requested availability for formal review slots.

2026-03-12 Priya Nair (Eng): Shared preliminary perf run results (internal dashboard link). Observed a 3.8% median token latency increase in the worst-case on-prem upgrade path; proposed kernel-selection fallback to avoid regressions for 95th percentile.

2026-03-12 Alex Morgan (Design): Submitted first-pass mockups for the upgrade flow and a11y checklist. Flagged edge-case: long-running upgrades need clearer progress feedback to prevent duplicate invocations.

2026-03-13 Samir Desai (Legal): Requested explicit language for audit log storage duration; flagged potential export-control question for certain APAC deployments. Legal suggests 2-week buffer for contract clause review.

2026-03-13 Jordan Patel (PM): Consolidated trade-offs: accept small perf increase with kernel fallback vs. extend dev work to eliminate perf hit. Propose canary rollout policy for initial customers to limit blast radius.
2026-03-14 Riley Chen: Scheduled cross-team approval meeting on 2026-03-18 15:00 PT and created the Confluence signoff checklist section. Added 'security_review_required' and linked runbook template.
